item.title: BlackRock’s Boivin Sees Rates Getting More in Line With the Environment
item.description: Jean Boivin, head of BlackRock Investment Institute, discusses the firm turning positive on US Treasuries, how the artificial intelligence buildout is influencing rates, and why long-term US Treasuries are “starting to be attractive.” He speaks on “Bloomberg Surveillance.” (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: OpenAI Targets $1.25 Trillion Valuation in New Funding Round
item.description:
A rout in the artificial intelligence trade faded, offering global stock investors some respite in the final session of a volatile week, with further gains in oil prices keeping sentiment cautious.
Bloomberg has learned OpenAI, which is seeking to raise around $30 billion in a fresh funding round, is now targeting a valuation of $1.25 trillion during the final stages of negotiations.
French authorities are bracing for a new round of protests Saturday, rolling out the military to back up police in a bid to prevent a repeat of last weekend’s riots and reassure markets unnerved by the violence.
Today's guests: Geoff Yu, BNY Senior Market Strategist; James Murray, Financial Secretary to the UK Treasury; Martin Quencez, German Marshall Fund of the United States Senior Fellow & Special Adviser to the President; Oskar Lewnowski, Orion Resource Partners Founder & Group CEO. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Dudley Sees Fed Likely to Hold With a Hike Coming in December
item.description: Bill Dudley, former New York Fed President and Bloomberg Opinion columnist, discusses messaging on interest rates from the Federal Reserve’s so-called troika, the influence of the artificial intelligence buildout on rates, and his expectation for the central bank to hold steady in October. His opinions are his own. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Futures Drop as Tech Stocks Slide, Oil Prices Climb Past $101 a Barrel
item.description: Futures fell on Friday with mixed trading in technology megacaps, oil climbing and US midterm elections less than two weeks away. Investors were parsing earnings from payments giant American Express Co. for signals about spending and the health of the economy.
item.dc:creator: Felice Maranz

item.title: The Forgotten Godmother of Economic Literature
item.description: In 1776, the field of economics was born with the publication of Adam Smith's The Wealth of Nations. Among the book's earliest readers was a Regency-era novelist named Maria Edgeworth. In her time, Edgeworth was one of the most famous literary figures in England, and she smuggled into her stories economic concepts and debates around rent seeking, the idea of productive labor, and so on. These works were enormously influential and they helped expose a generation to practical applications of Smith's theories. Jeanna Smialek, a veteran Fed reporter and the Brussels bureau chief at The New York Times, thinks Edgeworth's name needs to be placed back in the pantheon of economic history. Today, we discuss Edgeworth's friendly debates with the likes of Thomas Malthus and David Ricardo, how the Irish potato famine reshaped economic thought, and how Edgeworth used the novel form to educate the masses on the value of economics. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Hyperscalers Capex to Be Big 2027 Theme, UBS' Baweja Says
item.description: Bhanu Baweja, chief strategist at UBS Investment Bank, says spending by the largest hyperscalers will remain a major theme in markets in 2027. "At an aggregate level, I do not believe that there are major constraints here for hyperscalers," he tells Bloomberg Television, adding that they "will be rewarded." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Shoprite, Investec Said to Discuss South African Fintech Tie-Up
item.description: Shoprite Holdings Ltd. is said to be in talks with Investec about a partnership as Africa’s largest grocer seeks to expand the financial services it offers millions of customers, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Loni Prinsloo, Janice Kew and Adelaide Changole

item.title: AI Trade Faces Earnings Test: Market Snapshot
item.description: Some of the world's biggest tech names delivered earnings this week that drew mixed reactions from investors. The results come as jitters over the trade increasingly shift from cash flows and profits to how the technology’s massive build-out is being financed. "The Opening Trade" team spoke to market strategists and CEOs about whether this week's results suggest the artificial intelligence boom is nearing its peak, or still has room to run. (Source: Bloomberg)
